title.en: Doppler effect: a moving listener, the general formula and uses

hook.en: Drive towards a factory siren and its note rises; drive away and it falls. This time the source is still. You are running into the waves.

objectives.en: Find f′ for a moving listener
Combine both motions in one formula

say.en: Drive towards a factory siren and its note rises; drive away and it falls. This time the source is still. You are running into the waves. In this lesson: Find f′ for a moving listener.
Combine both motions in one formula.
Describe uses: radar, ultrasound, astronomy.

title.en: A moving listener meets more crests

body.en: When the source is still, the wavelength is unchanged, $\lambda = v/f$. A listener *moving* towards it at $v_o$ meets crests at the relative speed $v + v_o$, so $f' = f\,\dfrac{v + v_o}{v}$. Moving away: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v - v_o}{v}$. With both moving along the line joining them: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}$ (upper signs for approach). If the medium (wind) moves at $w$ from source to listener, replace $v$ by $v + w$.

points.en: Listener *moving*: same λ, more crests per second
Only velocity components along the line joining them count

narration.en: When the source is still, the wavelength is unchanged, $\lambda = v/f$. A listener moving towards it at $v_o$ meets crests at the relative speed $v + v_o$, so $f' = f\,\dfrac{v + v_o}{v}$. Moving away: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v - v_o}{v}$. With both moving along the line joining them: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}$ (upper signs for approach). If the medium (wind) moves at $w$ from source to listener, replace $v$ by $v + w$.

say.en: When the source is still, the wavelength is unchanged, lambda equals v over f. A listener moving towards it at v o meets crests at the relative speed v plus v o, so f' equals f v plus v o over v. Moving away: f' equals f v minus v o over v. With both moving along the line joining them: f' equals f v plus or minus v o over v minus or plus v s upper signs for approach. If the medium wind moves at w from source to listener, replace v by v plus w. Listener moving: same lambda, more crests per second.
General: f′ = f v plus or minus v o/(v ∓ v s).
Only velocity components along the line joining them count.

say.en: One formula for both motions.

body.en: A police radar sends waves at a car and measures the shift of the echo; the car acts first as a moving listener and then as a moving source, so the shift is about twice that for one motion. *Doppler* ultrasound measures the speed of blood in the heart. Bats judge their prey from the shift of their echoes. Light from galaxies moving away is shifted to longer wavelengths (red shift).

points.en: Echo from a *moving* reflector: two shifts

problem.en: A car moving at 30 m/s approaches a stationary siren of 660 Hz. What frequency does the driver hear? (v = 330 m/s)

steps.en: The listener moves towards a still source: f' = f (v + v_o)/v.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A car moving at 30 m/s approaches a stationary siren of 660 Hz. What frequency does the driver hear? (v = 330 m/s)

say.en: Let us solve this together. A car moving at 30 metres per second approaches a stationary siren of 660 hertz. What frequency does the driver hear? (v equals 330 metres per second).
The listener moves towards a still source: f' = f v plus v o/v.
f' = 660 times 360 over 330 equals 720 hertz.
So the answer is 720 hertz.

problem.en: A car sounding a 400 Hz horn moves at 20 m/s towards a wall. What is the frequency of the echo heard by the driver? (v = 340 m/s)

steps.en: The wall re-emits 425 Hz; the driver moves towards it: f₂ = 425 × (340 + 20)/340 = 450 Hz.
In one step: f₂ = f (v + u)/(v − u) = 400 × 360/320.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A car sounding a 400 Hz horn moves at 20 m/s towards a wall. What is the frequency of the echo heard by the driver? (v = 340 m/s)

say.en: Let us solve this together. A car sounding a 400 hertz horn moves at 20 metres per second towards a wall. What is the frequency of the echo heard by the driver? (v equals 340 metres per second).
The wall hears f 1 equals 400 times 340 over 340 minus 20 equals 425 hertz.
The wall re-emits 425 hertz; the driver moves towards it: f 2 equals 425 times 340 plus 20/340 equals 450 hertz.
In one step: f 2 equals f v plus u/(v - u) equals 400 times 360 over 320.
So the answer is 450 hertz.

body.en: For an echo from a fixed wall when you move at u: f_echo = f (v + u)/(v − u). For small u, the shift is about 2u/v of f.
